proposals.before: On the jiwei day, the Prince of Zheng Chonggui, Prince of Kaifeng and Administrator of the Kaifeng Prefecture; Liu Zhiyuan, Military Governor of the Guide Army and Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard Horse and Foot; and Du Chongwei, Military Governor of the Zhongwu Army—all were promoted to Grand Councilor with the Concurrent Signatory of the Secretariat.
proposals.after: On the jiwei day, the imperial son Chonggui, Prince of Zheng and Administrator of Kaifeng; Liu Zhiyuan, Military Governor of the Guide Army and Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard Horse and Foot; and Du Chongwei, Military Governor of the Zhongwu Army—all were promoted to Grand Councilor with the Concurrent Signatory of the Secretariat.
proposals.reason: Chinese 開封尹 is the Kaifeng prefectural administrator office, not a second princely title “Prince of Kaifeng”; 皇子 goes with 重貴.

proposals.before: On the dingwei day, Long Min, deputy military commissioner of the Western Capital, was appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
proposals.after: On the dingwei day, Long Min, deputy stay-behind commissioner of the Western Capital, was appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
proposals.reason: 西京副留守 is the deputy capital stay-behind/guardian post, not a “deputy military commissioner.”

proposals.before: On the dingchou day, Wu Chengfang was transferred to secretariat drafter and made Hanlin academician;
proposals.after: On the dingchou day, Wu Chengfan was transferred to secretariat drafter and made Hanlin academician;
proposals.reason: Chinese 吳承範 is Wu Chengfan (範 fàn); Chengfang misreads the given name.

proposals.before: On the dingchou day, Wu Chengfang, Director of the Sacrificial Section and drafter of edicts, was transferred to Secretariat Drafter and made Hanlin Academician;
proposals.after: On the dingchou day, Wu Chengfan, Director of the Sacrificial Section and drafter of edicts, was transferred to Secretariat Drafter and made Hanlin Academician;
proposals.reason: Chinese 吳承範 is Wu Chengfan (範 fàn); Chengfang misreads the given name.

proposals.before: and Cui Wan was transferred to chief minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
proposals.after: and Cui Zhuo was transferred to chief minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
proposals.reason: Chinese 崔棁 is Cui Zhuo (棁 zhuō); Wan is not a valid reading of 棁.

proposals.before: Cui Wan, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was transferred to Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
proposals.after: Cui Zhuo, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was transferred to Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
proposals.reason: Chinese 崔棁 is Cui Zhuo (棁 zhuō); Wan is not a valid reading of 棁.

proposals.before: On the jihai day, Lady Zhang, widow of the late Prince Chongying, took the tonsure as a nun; she was given the name Wushen and twenty summer fast days.
proposals.after: On the jihai day, Lady Zhang, widow of the late Prince Chongying, took the tonsure as a nun; she was given the name Wushen and twenty summers of monastic age.
proposals.reason: 夏臘 counts years since tonsure (monastic summers), not summer fast days.

proposals.before: On the jihai day, Lady Zhang, wife of the late Prince Chongying, shaved her head and became a nun; she was granted the name Wushen and also given twenty summer fast days.
proposals.after: On the jihai day, Lady Zhang, wife of the late Prince Chongying, shaved her head and became a nun; she was granted the name Wushen and also given twenty summers of monastic age.
proposals.reason: 夏臘 counts years since tonsure (monastic summers), not summer fast days.

proposals.before: On the bingchen day, an edict forbade the construction of new Buddhist and Daoist monastic compounds in cities, villages, and wards.
proposals.after: On the bingchen day, an edict forbade the construction of new Buddhist monk and nun monastic compounds in cities, villages, and wards.
proposals.reason: 僧尼 means Buddhist monks and nuns; the Chinese does not mention Daoists.

proposals.before: On the bingchen day, an edict stated that henceforth in walled cities, villages, and wards, Buddhist and Daoist monastic compounds must not be newly built.
proposals.after: On the bingchen day, an edict stated that henceforth in walled cities, villages, and wards, Buddhist monk and nun monastic compounds must not be newly built.
proposals.reason: 僧尼 means Buddhist monks and nuns; the Chinese does not mention Daoists.

decisions.reason: 皇子 identifies Chonggui as an imperial son, while 開封尹 is his administrative office; it is not a second princely title.
西京副留守 is deputy stay-behind commissioner of the Western Capital, not a military commissionership.
The given name 承範 is Chengfan; Chengfang is a misreading of 範.
The literal field must likewise render 吳承範 as Wu Chengfan.
The personal name 崔棁 is read Cui Zhuo; Wan is not a reading of 棁.
The literal field must likewise render 崔棁 as Cui Zhuo.
夏臘 is a Buddhist measure of seniority counted in summers since ordination, not a number of fast days.
The literal field also mistakes monastic seniority, 夏臘, for summer fast days.

decisions.after: On the bingchen day, an edict forbade the construction of new Buddhist monasteries and nunneries in cities, villages, and wards.
decisions.reason: 僧尼 means Buddhist monks and nuns and contains no Daoist reference; 'monasteries and nunneries' is the natural idiomatic rendering of their 院舍.

decisions.after: On the bingchen day, an edict stated that henceforth no new compounds for Buddhist monks or nuns were to be built in walled cities, villages, or wards.
decisions.reason: The literal field invents Daoists; 僧尼 refers specifically to Buddhist monks and nuns.
